_comment: Services whose container health signal cannot go red for a real outage, recorded
rather than quietly tolerated. scripts/check_health_claims.py enforces the shape:
an entry with no reason, no owner, or a past expiry is itself a failure, because a
stale waiver is another claim nobody checks.
2026-07-26: the KERNEL waiver is GONE - not renewed, discharged. Its healthcheck now
probes /readyz. The deferral was written around a coupling that measurement showed is
not real: stopping the fleet-worker does NOT flip the kernel unhealthy, because the
stack-tool receipt is cached in Redis. What IS real is hatchet - stopping the engine
does flip it - and that was accepted, because durable execution is a required
readiness check and a kernel without it genuinely is not ready. Rehearsed on dev
first: forcing the schema head to 0037 made the container unhealthy while /healthz
kept answering 200, which is the 2026-07-25 client outage reproduced and caught.

fleet-worker.reason: The probe is `python -c "import boltrig"`, which proves the interpreter can import a module and nothing else - not that the pump is claiming work, not that it can reach the store. It is exempt rather than fixed because `python -m boltrig.api.worker` serves no HTTP at all, so there is no readiness endpoint to point at; inventing a requirement it cannot satisfy would make the gate a lie in the other direction. It is not exempt from the GOAL: it already publishes a signed, short-lived stack-tool receipt to Redis that the kernel's /readyz consumes, so the real fix is a `boltrig fleet health` command that reads that receipt and exits non-zero when it is stale or absent.
